# Modern laser tag. Built like a video game. Built to make you money.

Battle Company systems bring the games your guests already play into a live arena. That means weapon swaps, kill streaks, objectives, and live scoring, all run by one staff member from a tablet.

[Book a Live Demo](https://battlecompany.com/laser-tag/#bc-form) [Call 888.798.9616](tel:+18887989616)

Building laser tag since 2012. Sold in 40+ countries and all 50 states. Designed, built, and supported in Oak Creek, WI.

![Player wearing a Battle Company headset aims a Battle Rifle Pro next to a Utility Box in an indoor arena](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

## See It in Action

This isn’t your parents’ laser tag. It’s live-action gaming.

## Why Operators Choose Battle Company

### Games guests come back for

EDGE comes loaded with preset games, weapons, abilities, and melee attacks, and you can build unlimited games of your own.

### Easy to run

One employee runs the whole arena from a tablet with EDGE Terminal.

### Runs anywhere

It needs power, not internet, so it works indoors, outdoors, and even off a generator.

### Built to last

The shells are polymer nylon-fiberglass, and we’ve never seen one broken in gameplay. Parts are modular, so you only pay for what breaks.

### Made in the USA, supported in-house

Our own team handles design, onboarding, repairs, and support.

## Pick Your Gear

![Battle Rifle Pro laser tag rifle with reflex sight](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Battle Rifle Pro

Our flagship and our most popular commercial unit. It’s light and durable, and every age loves it.

![Battle Rifle XL laser tag rifle](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Battle Rifle XL

The Pro with extra length for adult players, plus a removable mag.

![BRM laser tag rifle with magazine](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### BRM

The most realistic unit on the market, with a metal hybrid body, battery-powered recoil, a flip mag, and a charge handle.

![Alternator laser tag blaster shown in rifle and SMG configurations](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Alternator

Compact and family-friendly, for younger players. Switching the stock swaps weapons.

**Which one fits your guests?** [Get a Recommendation](https://battlecompany.com/laser-tag/#bc-form)

## What is Mobile Laser Tag?

Take Battle Company on the road. The same system that powers arenas also works for mobile businesses, indoors, outdoors, and even off a generator.

[Ask About Mobile Setups](https://battlecompany.com/laser-tag/#bc-form)

## Gear That Changes the Game

![Battle Company wireless headset](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Wireless 360° Headset

Sensors on both the headset and the gun mean no cheating, and it unlocks healing, splash damage, and melee.

![Plug-in reflex red dot sight](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Powered Reflex Sight

The sight runs off the gun’s battery. Its reticle flips red and green to confirm hits, just like in a video game.

![Battle Company Utility Box](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Utility Box

It has 25+ modes, including respawn, weapon upgrades, medic, ammo, flags, and capture points. Players can shoot it or press its button, and it can ping players nearby. It also triggers lights, fog, and sound.

![IR grenade held in hand, showing removable charge handle and fuse button](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)![Shock band worn on a wrist](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### IR Grenade & Shock Band

Two upsells that make big groups and corporate events unforgettable.

![Child throwing a ball at a Bullseye Smart Target with the EDGE score screen in the background](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

### Bullseye Smart Target

Brings EDGE scoring to balls, darts, and foam blasters.

## EDGE: The Most Powerful Laser Tag Software in the Industry

Load a game in one click, fill the lobby, and hit start. Save game lists for birthdays, corporate events, and open play, so every group gets the same great experience every time. After each game, players get medals for MVP, Sharp Shooter, and Trigger Happy.

**Callsign app:** Players track their stats, level up, and unlock rewards you choose, and you can send them promos and loot boxes. That keeps them coming back.

![EDGE post-game medal screen](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

![EDGE live scoreboard during a Capture the Flag game](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

![Phone showing the Callsign app with a Download the Free App banner](https://battlecompany.com/wp-content/plugins/wp-fastest-cache-premium/pro/images/blank.gif)

Family entertainment centersBowling centersTrampoline parksCampgroundsHauntsMobile businessesUniversitiesMilitary training

Birthday partiesCorporate team buildingPost-prom and homecomingYouth groupsHalloweenFundraisers

## Trusted By

Universal Studios Singapore · Urban Air · Knott’s · Herschend Live · Europa-Park · Kalahari · Trans Studio · Jellystone · Halo Outpost Discovery, plus every branch of the U.S. military.

### Design-build

Our team designs high-throughput arenas, from a refresh of an existing center to a branded attraction.

### Onboarding

Remote training is included, and in-person and on-site training are available.

### Support

Tickets, a phone line, a customer portal, a parts shop, and an RMA repair service.

Upgrade to Battle Company. You get more guns, EDGE, and service. Add Flash Pads on leftover floor or Pixel Putt for open space.

# How to layout your entertainment space

[Knowledge Hub](https://blog.lasertag.com/tag/knowledge-hub) [Designing an Experience they won't forget](https://blog.lasertag.com/tag/designing-an-experience-they-wont-forget) Feb 15, 2022 10:23:05 AM [Grant Collins](https://blog.lasertag.com/author/grant) 2 min read

![](https://blog.lasertag.com/hs-fs/hubfs/LineofsiteMap-01.png?width=1000&name=LineofsiteMap-01.png)

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet/?text=How+to+layout+your+entertainment+space&url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.lasertag.com%2Fhow-to-layout-your-entertainment-space)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.lasertag.com%2Fhow-to-layout-your-entertainment-space)[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.lasertag.com%2Fhow-to-layout-your-entertainment-space)[](mailto:?subject=How%20to%20layout%20your%20entertainment%20space&body=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.lasertag.com%2Fhow-to-layout-your-entertainment-space)

Planning how all your attractions will fit together, and not waste your space (where every bit costs you) but also not feel too claustrophobic is essential to creating the welcoming feel you're aiming for! But how do you do this?  
  
The first step is to create a mock it up on cardboard, to whatever scale you can practically play around with, making sure to mark in any fixed objects that aren't negotiable ie Supporting Pillars. Then cut each attraction out of a different bit of card so they can easily be moved around within the space. Then explore options, move them around see what feels right before modelling the space in Sketchup or Cad.  
Paying particular attention to site lines from where your staff will be placed, in a quick example;  
![Vision Map-01](https://blog.lasertag.com/hs-fs/hubfs/Vision%20Map-01.jpg?width=461&name=Vision%20Map-01.jpg)  
If the counter was in black, and attractions laid like this. There would be multiple potential spots, with the counter unable to see 3 of your attractions! (Vision marked in grey) Each blind spot potentially means more staff needed to man the attractions, so more ongoing costs.  
  
Once the site lines are more or less sorted, draw foot traffic, to see a heat map, ie where do guests go-between attractions, can they easily find bathrooms, where are the potential choke points.  
  
Drawing each customer potential journey, then overlaying with the next and the next, so you can see heat maps of where there are busy areas, cutovers and more. This will allow you to ensure that the circulation passageway through the spaces follows an easy and economic pathway from the door to all the other main activity areas.

In terms of overall design, there are a lot of things to consider;

*   Do you change floor types between areas to signify the activity, or do you use lighting to do this?
*   If you want them to feel separate, floor is a good way to do so. Conversely, if you use the same floor style in two spaces adjacent to each other, they both feel larger as you’re more or less borrowing some of the space from the adjoining attraction.
*   When planning decoration and lighting, work with the principles that vertical lines draw our eyes up and horizontal lines draw them across to extend or reduce the proportions of a room. Angles bring focus to what they lean towards. These work in combination, so light is a great way to create focal points within the space.
*   Perception of space is based on body size. Different size spaces suit different size people: one person’s claustrophobic box is another’s cosy nest. So make sure you consider each space, and passage from the height of a child to a 6 foot adult. Along with wheelchairs, larger builds and all the in-betweens. Ie if your fence around an attraction is 1.2M, kids can’t see over it, so consider using some glass windows/separations so they can see what is on the other side.
*   Some attractions ie Laser Tag are concealed in a space, others like bumpers are low lying so can easily be seen over, so consider the heights and nature of the attractions during the placement phase.
*   Some attractions are required to be X shape ie bowling, others like gokarts/laser can be multiple so I’d start with the fixed space attractions, then do the ones that can be more flexible. Some have requirements ie Plumbing, ventilations, so try and make sure that these are in logical places to each other as well.

To learn more about specifically designing a Laser Tag Centre layout, please read [our more detailed guide](https://lasertag.com/laser-tag-facility-layout/)
